examDifficulty.heading: Is the Health Cloud Accredited Professional Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam covers Health Cloud’s patient and clinical data model, care coordination and connections to healthcare systems. Know how the org represents patients before selecting related records.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 90 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
Check the current official exam guide for the passing score; do not infer it from a practice test.
Data model focus. Patients, care teams, care plans and the clinical objects based on FHIR.
Industry processes. Care management, appointments, utilisation management and data integration.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Use practice questions to find gaps, then check the current exam guide and Salesforce Help for product behavior. A practice score is a study aid, not a promise of an exam result.

examFormat.heading: Health Cloud Accredited Professional Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are taken online. Check the current exam guide for the latest details.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Scenarios describe a patient, provider or care-team need. Identify the record or process involved, and account for the organization’s patient model and data integrations.
bestWayToPass: Confirm how the implementation represents patients and clinical records.
Review care plans, care teams, patient timelines and appointment workflows.
Understand the role of FHIR and the organization’s EHR integration.
Treat access controls, encryption and audit requirements as part of the design.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers Health Cloud’s patient and clinical data model, care plans and teams, appointments, utilization management and integrations. The exam is 60 scored questions in 90 minutes, with a 63% pass mark, weighted towards Design and Implement (42% each).

keyConcepts.h2: Health Cloud: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Health Cloud Data Model: Patients, Providers, and Care Plans
blocks.body: Health Cloud can represent patients, providers, facilities and care relationships. Some orgs use person accounts for patients; the patient model depends on the implementation. Clinical data objects can represent items such as conditions, medications, observations and encounters, with data aligned to healthcare standards such as FHIR. The patient timeline presents related events in date order.

blocks.heading: Care Plan Management and Coordination
blocks.body: A care plan organizes a patient’s problems, goals, and the tasks or interventions needed to address them. Teams can start with a template, assign work, track progress, and update the plan. Assessments can supply information for care planning.

blocks.heading: Intelligent Appointment Management (IAM)
blocks.body: Intelligent appointment management helps match appointments to provider availability, skills, and location. Depending on the setup, patients can book through self-service and receive reminders or confirmations. Appointments can be connected to the patient record.

blocks.heading: FHIR Integration and EHR Connectivity
blocks.body: Clinical records often live in an electronic health record system. Health Cloud can exchange relevant information through integrations, including FHIR-based APIs and MuleSoft healthcare accelerators. Design the flow around the system of record and the information care teams need.

blocks.heading: Analytics and Population Health Management
blocks.body: Reports, dashboards, and CRM Analytics can help teams identify groups that need follow-up, such as patients due for a check-up. Utilization management supports review of care requests against criteria. Protect health information with appropriate sharing, field security, encryption, monitoring, and applicable privacy controls.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Health Cloud Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Identify the patient or provider need, then trace it to the correct care record or process.

blocks.heading: Confirm the patient model
blocks.body: Health Cloud implementations may represent patients differently; follow the org’s configured model.

blocks.heading: Build care around the patient
blocks.body: Care plans organize needs, goals and tasks; care teams identify the people supporting the patient.

blocks.heading: Use clinical data records
blocks.body: Choose the appropriate condition, medication, observation or encounter record for the data.

blocks.heading: Keep the EHR relationship clear
blocks.body: Know which system is authoritative and how the integration transfers the data care teams need.

blocks.heading: Review access before sharing
blocks.body: Use permissions and sharing settings to limit sensitive health records to appropriate users.

nextCertsAfter.intro: Good next steps after Health Cloud:

sampleQuestions.question: Which Health Cloud feature lists the people involved in a patient’s care and their roles?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Care Team is the best fit because the care team lists the people involved in a patient's care, each with their role.
whyWrong: An Opportunity Team is not the best choice because opportunity teams are for sales deals.
The patient’s household is not the best choice because households group people who share finances, not care roles.
A Price Book is not the best choice because price books hold product prices.

sampleQuestions.question: What can a coordinator create to organize a patient’s recovery goals and tasks?
options: Create a Lead for the patient
Create a Campaign for the discharge
Use a standard Case without a care plan
sampleQuestions.explanation: Template-based Care Plan is the best fit because care plans set out problems, goals and tasks, and templates make them quick and consistent to create.
whyWrong: Create a Lead for the patient is not the best choice because leads are for sales.
Create a Campaign for the discharge is not the best choice because campaigns are for marketing.
Use a standard Case without a care plan is not the best choice because a Case tracks an issue, but doesn't structure goals and tasks.

sampleQuestions.question: Which standard informs Health Cloud’s clinical data model?
sampleQuestions.explanation: FHIR is the best fit because health Cloud's clinical data model is aligned with FHIR, the common standard for exchanging health data.
whyWrong: OAuth is not the best choice because oAuth is for authorising app access.
SOAP is not the best choice because sOAP is a web service protocol, not a health data standard.
SAML is not the best choice because sAML is for single sign-on.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Health Cloud record is suited to a blood-pressure measurement?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Care Observation is the best fit because care observations record measurements like blood pressure or blood sugar.
whyWrong: Care Team Role is not the best choice because care team roles describe people's roles.
Account-Contact Relationship is not the best choice because that links people to accounts.
Care Plan Template is not the best choice because templates define standard plans.

sampleQuestions.question: If the EHR remains the clinical source of truth, how can Health Cloud receive needed data?
sampleQuestions.explanation: FHIR integration is the best fit because integration brings clinical data in automatically, while the EHR stays the source of truth.
whyWrong: Replace the EHR is not the best choice because retyping is slow and causes errors.
Ask nurses to retype records is not the best choice because pDFs can't be used as structured data.
Email record PDFs is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Integrate with the EHR using FHIR APIs.

sampleQuestions.question: Which capability supports patient self-service appointment booking with an appropriate provider?
options: Price Book for provider services and rates
Chatter group for patient booking requests
Web-to-Lead form for new patient referrals
sampleQuestions.explanation: Intelligent Appointment Management is the best fit because intelligent appointment management matches patients with providers by availability, skills and location, including self-service booking.
whyWrong: Price Book for provider services and rates is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Intelligent Appointment Management.
Chatter group for patient booking requests is not the best choice because chatter groups are for collaboration.
Web-to-Lead form for new patient referrals is not the best choice because web-to-lead captures sales leads.

sampleQuestions.question: Which view presents a patient’s visits, results and other events in date order?
options: Build a dashboard for every patient
Open the Patient Timeline for ordered events
Create a report instead of using the timeline
sampleQuestions.explanation: Open the Patient Timeline for ordered events is the best fit because the timeline shows a patient's events in order on their record.
whyWrong: Build a dashboard for every patient is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Open the Patient Timeline for ordered events.
Review the Setup Audit Trail is not the best choice because audit Trail tracks setup changes.
Create a report instead of using the timeline is not the best choice because building a report each time is slow.

sampleQuestions.question: Which process handles clinical requests that need coverage review, such as an MRI?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Utilization request is the best fit because utilization management handles prior authorisation through care requests that reviewers assess.
whyWrong: Campaign is not the best choice because lead conversion is for sales.
Lead conversion is not the best choice because action plans list tasks but don't run the approval review.
Action Plan alone is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Utilization Management request.

sampleQuestions.question: How can a clinic identify diabetic patients who have not had a recent check-up?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Report on conditions and encounters is the best fit because reports and analytics on clinical data can find groups of patients who need follow-up.
whyWrong: Search Chatter is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Report on conditions and encounters.
Ask clinicians to remember is not the best choice because memory is unreliable.
Open every patient record manually is not the best choice because checking by hand doesn't scale.

sampleQuestions.question: Which controls help protect sensitive health information in Health Cloud?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data access controls is the best fit because health data needs tight access control, encryption and records of who accessed what.
whyWrong: Set sharing to Public Read/Write is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Restrict sharing, encrypt data and audit access.
Use one shared staff login is not the best choice because shared logins remove accountability.
Store records in Chatter is not the best choice because chatter isn't a secure store for clinical data.

sampleQuestions.question: How should a coordinator handle an extra task needed for one patient but absent from the standard plan?
options: Change the template for every patient
sampleQuestions.explanation: Patient-specific care-plan task is the best fit because care plans start from templates but can be adjusted for each patient.
whyWrong: Create a new org is not the best choice because changing the template affects every future plan.
Change the template for every patient is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Add the extra task to that patient’s care plan.
Delete the care plan is not the best choice because deleting loses the plan.

sampleQuestions.question: Which kind of Health Cloud record holds a patient’s medication information?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Medication records is the best fit because health Cloud has clinical objects for medications, aligned to FHIR.
whyWrong: Price Book Entry is not the best choice because campaign members are for marketing.
Campaign Member is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Clinical medication records.
Opportunity Product is not the best choice because opportunity products are for sales.

sampleQuestions.question: How might an implementation represent an individual patient?
options: Create a Product record for the patient
Create a Lead for each patient
Create a Salesforce User for each patient
sampleQuestions.explanation: Person Account is the best fit because person accounts combine account and contact details for an individual, which fits patients.
whyWrong: Create a Product record for the patient is not the best choice because products are things that are sold.
Create a Lead for each patient is not the best choice because leads are prospects.
Create a Salesforce User for each patient is not the best choice because users log in to Salesforce.

sampleQuestions.question: How can patient assessment answers support care planning?
options: Use the answers only for marketing
sampleQuestions.explanation: Assessment results guide care is the best fit because assessment answers help coordinators spot needs and shape the care plan.
whyWrong: Replace the EHR is not the best choice because price books are unrelated.
Change the Price Book is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Use the responses to inform care-plan goals.
Use the answers only for marketing is not the best choice because they are for care, not marketing.

sampleQuestions.question: Which records can represent providers, their networks and specialties?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Provider-network records is the best fit because health Cloud can store providers, facilities, specialties and networks for referrals and scheduling.
whyWrong: Campaign hierarchy for network promotions is not the best choice because opportunity stages track deals.
Opportunity stages is not the best choice because email templates format messages.
Email templates is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Provider and network records.
